Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-28
Start: 16:00 PT

Attendees: Marcus Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Alicia Gomez (Cedar - Procurement), Daniel Cho (Cedar - Dir Security), Meera Patel (Cedar - Legal), Samir Khan (Cedar - Eng Lead)

Summary (auto):
Quick commercial + legal alignment for privileged onboarding. Discussed SLA commitments for Dedicated vs Private, DPA redlines (data retention, subprocessors, audit logs), KMS integration, SSO, pricing tiers and pilot commitment. Transcript:
[00:00] Marcus: okay, uh hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Marcus with Redwood, i'm the AE on this account, quick roll call?
[00:12] Alicia: hi, Alicia here from procurement, thanks Marcus.
[00:16] Daniel: Daniel Cho, security.
[00:18] Meera: Meera Patel, legal.
[00:20] Samir: Samir, eng.
[00:22] Priya: Priya from Redwood, i'll drive the technical bits today.
[00:26] Marcus: awesome. Goal for today is to align on the SLA / DPA / pricing tradeoffs for Cedar's privileged workload pilot. We got your RFP notes earlier Alicia, thanks. Quick context question — Samir, can you say briefly the shape of traffic and the privacy constraints?
[00:44] Samir: yeah sure. We're mostly synchronous inference calls from our internal assistant, peak QPS around 120 for the pilot, median payload about 512 tokens, spikes to 2k tokens for long document context. All PII redaction happens client-side, but we still need strong data residency and audit logs. Also, no customer data can leave the EU region for EU tenants, that's key.
[01:10] Priya: got it. So two primary constraints — region residency and auditability. For residency we can do Redwood Private (VPC) deployed into your cloud region or on-prem if needed. For audit logs we have per-request immutable traces and an audit export for SIEM. Note: the export is S3-compatible and we can route to your logging account.
[01:34] Daniel: when you say audit export, is it token-level or just request metadata? We need to confirm because compliance wants no raw content in logs.
[01:44] Priya: good point. Our default export includes metadata and timing, and can include hashes of request payloads. We don't store plaintext by default unless customer enables retention. There's a configuration flag.
[01:58] Daniel: ok please send docs on config flags. Also KMS — we need to use our KMS or HSM and have envelope keys.
[02:07] Priya: yes, we integrate with customer-managed keys (KM S) — sorry, KMS — and we support both cloud KMS and BYOHSM. For the private deployment we can do in-line envelope encryption and we do not persist plaintext keys. There's an extra egress and ops note there.
[02:26] Meera: on the DPA side, our lawyers will want to see subprocessors and a liability cap aligned with our procurement guidelines. We had some redlines to indemnity and export controls in the RFP.
[02:38] Marcus: totally, Meera. We usually provide our standard DPA and list of subprocessors; Priya will attach SOC2 and the subprocessor list. For caps, i want to set expectations — Redwood typically aligns to market for SaaS vendors. If you have specific thresholds we can surface them to our legal.
[02:54] Meera: i'll compile the top five exceptions.
[02:58] [00:60] Alicia: pricing — we're evaluating per-token hosted vs a reserved dedicated pool. Can you outline the pricing delta and which makes sense for a pilot?
[03:12] Marcus: yes. Short answer: hosted is fastest to start, pay-as-you-go; dedicated/reserved is cheaper at scale and gives isolation. For the pilot (3 months, expected steady QPS ~80), dedicated capacity with burst is often preferred because it's predictable for finops. We'll send scenarios.
[03:31] Samir: on dedicated, what's the failover story? If a node fails do we get transparent fallback to hosted? We can't have downtime.
[03:40] Priya: good question. We support smart routing: can fall back to hosted variants automatically, policy-driven. There is a small latency penalty on fallback plus potential model variant differences, but we can configure canary fallback policies and automatic traffic shifting. For 99.9 SLO we recommend reserved pools with cross-zone redundancy.
[03:58] Daniel: SLO specifics? We're looking for 99th percentile token latency under 200ms for v1 of the pilot, and 99.9 availability. Is that doable?
[04:10] Priya: under typical conditions yes for shorter sequences; for 2k-token tails latency grows. We can set per-route SLOs and provide token-level tracing to prove compliance. For long sequences we recommend an optimized quantized model profile and prefix KV caching to reduce re-compute.
[04:30] Samir: prefix K-V cash?
[04:33] Priya: K-V cache, sorry, the KV cache — the key-value cache used for autoregressive states.
[04:36] Samir: got it. The RFP also mentions egress fees — how do those work for private?
[04:42] Marcus: egress depends on whether data crosses accounts/regions. For Private in your VPC, egress is minimal between services in-region. If we route logs to your S3 account, there's no third-party egress fee from Redwood, but your cloud provider egress could apply if cross-region. We'll note this in the pricing worksheet.
[05:00] Alicia: procurement needs a cadence — after we see pricing & legal we have a procurement review on 2026-02-16. Can we align deliverables?
[05:08] Marcus: yes — we'll aim to have pricing & docs in your hands by 02-02 so you have time.
[05:12] [06:00] Meera: there was an ask in the RFP about escrow for models and continuity in case of acquisition. Is that standard?
[05:22] Marcus: escrow is not standard but we've done it for some enterprise customers. We keep a list of model artifacts and a continuity plan, and we can negotiate escrow or an EOL commitment. That will affect price.
[05:38] Meera: okay add that to the redline item list.
[05:42] [07:00] Priya: technical note — for private we provide a thin control plane from Redwood and the data plane in your VPC. For on-prem we ship an operator and runbooks. For the pilot I suggest private VPC deployment into your account with customer KMS and SSO. That usually hits procurement & security sweet spot.
[06:09] Daniel: SSO — we need SAML and SCIM for provisioning and SSO session length control. Will Redwood integrate with our Okta?
[06:18] Priya: yes Okta via SAML + SCIM provisioning is supported. We'll share the SSO integration guide.
[06:22] Samir: what's the monitoring surface? We need token-level cost, latencies, per-route dashboards and traces.
[06:29] Lena: that's our console — per-route dashboards, token cost breakdown, traces and alerting hooks. We can create a dedicated project view for Cedar so procurement and engineering see separate dashboards.
[06:40] Alicia: procurement will want a 30/60/90 day cost projection and a simple one-page commercial with committed spend tiers.
[06:47] Marcus: we'll include committed tiers with monthly burn rates and overage terms. Also optional burst pricing.
[06:52] [10:00] Meera: on data retention and DPA — we have strict rules about retention beyond 30 days and need the ability to purge records on demand and to get proof of deletion. How does Redwood handle that?
[07:12] Priya: we support data deletion requests and can provide attestations. For private you control retention settings. For hosted we have a retention flag and deletion API and we can produce deletion proofs in logs. We'll include the API docs.
[07:28] Daniel: also need SOC 2 type 2 and penetration test results.
[07:32] Marcus: Priya will push SOC2 and pen test abstracts; full reports can be shared under NDA.
[07:38] Priya: yes, i have the SOC2 summary and our latest pen test high-level; i'll attach.
[07:42] Samir: what about model updates and rollouts — we need canarying and the ability to pin model versions for regulatory reasons.
[07:49] Priya: models can be pinned per-route; rollouts use canary policies and automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts. For private we mirror the same APIs.
[07:59] Alicia: okay, good. Pricing question again — what about committed minimums for reserved capacity? Procurement tolerance is around 3-6 month commitments.
[08:08] Marcus: typical reserved contracts start at 3 months for pilots, 12 months for production. We'll show a 3-month pilot reserved price and a 12-month committed discount.
[08:18] Meera: for the DPA, one exception is our data export clause — we require subprocessor notification 30 days in advance. Any issues with that?
[08:26] Marcus: we can negotiate notification windows, but some cloud infra subprocessors are standard and subject to cloud provider terms. We'll call those out.
[08:34] Meera: would Redwood accept a reasonable carve-out for cloud infra?
[08:37] Marcus: yes, we'll propose standard cloud infra carve-outs and list them.
[08:40] [12:00] Alicia: procurement will want to know if we can start onboarding with a PO for the pilot. Do you accept PO-based payments?
[08:54] Marcus: we accept PO and invoice for enterprise deals; for pilot purchases we sometimes accept corporate card or invoice — we'll include payment terms.
[09:02] Samir: are there any material compliance gaps? FedRAMP? We're not asking FedRAMP yet but curious for the roadmap.
[09:09] Priya: roadmap includes FedRAMP consideration for 2026+ for certain deployments. For now SOC2 + pen tests + private VPC with customer KMS is our recommended path.
[09:20] Daniel: what about export controls (crypto, data transfer) — red flag for us if models or logs could be transferred outside the EU.
[09:28] Priya: we'll ensure region pinning for data plane and logs. For hosted fallback we can restrict fallback outside region. We'll document the technical knobs.
[09:38] Meera: also need a clause about audit rights for our security team.
[09:42] Marcus: we do standard audit cooperation with notice; full on-site audits are handled on a case-by-case basis.
[09:48] [15:00] Alicia: procurement timeline — assuming we get pricing and DPA by 02-02, procurement review 02-16, legal exchange 02-10, can we target a kickoff on 02-22?
[09:58] Marcus: yes that's realistic. That gives us time to prep the environment.
[10:02] Priya: for the benchmark, we'll need a small dataset and sample traffic. Samir, can you provide sample request traces and token distributions?
[10:10] Samir: yes i'll attach a sanitized traffic dump and sample sequences.
[10:14] Priya: perfect. We'll run the benchmark in your VPC with metrics and a short report.
[10:20] [19:00] Meera: last legal question — liability caps for data breaches, can we get a bump if we're sharing sensitive financial PII?
[10:32] Marcus: we can escalate to legal, typically liability caps map to subscription size or enterprise tier. We'll have our legal team propose language.
[10:38] Meera: also need to confirm that Redwood will not be a data controller.
[10:42] Marcus: we state data processor in the DPA; legal will confirm exact phrasing.
[10:46] [22:00] Priya: quick demo note — the console can show token level cost, route SLOs and a per-token latency waterfall. Lena, do you want to highlight any observability screenshots?
[10:58] Lena: yes i'll include a sample dashboard export in the follow-up.
[11:02] Alicia: ok i'm seeing alignment — commercial, security, legal, technical. Anything unresolved?
[11:08] Samir: just the benchmark specifics and the exact SLOs for 2k-token tails.
[11:12] Priya: we'll propose two SLO tiers: 0-512 tokens 99th < 200ms; tail up to 2k we provide 99th < 800ms with recommended batching/quantization. We'll document.
[11:26] [28:00] Marcus: recap of next steps — Marcus sends pricing worksheet; Priya shares SOC2, DPA draft, SSO + KMS notes; Samir supplies traffic sample; Meera compiles redlines; schedule benchmark week of 02-08; legal exchange by 02-10; procurement review 02-16; target onboarding kickoff 02-22.
[11:56] Alicia: sounds good. One more ask: can you provide an example MSA term sheet? Procurement prefers a one-pager.
[12:04] Marcus: yes we'll provide a term sheet and a one-page commercial.
[12:08] Meera: do you have a contact in legal for us to send redlines?
[12:12] Marcus: yes that's Jenna Cole in our legal ops — i'll cc her in the follow-up.
[12:16] [32:00] Priya: ok i'll get the DPA and SOC2 and include notes on KMS integration and the deletion API.
[12:24] Samir: and i'll prep sample traces by end of week.
[12:28] Marcus: thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and pricing later today/tomorrow.
